headline: X settles multiyear legal battle with advertisers over brand safety concerns
summary: The social media platform and the World Federation of Advertisers have agreed to end litigation that began after X sued the WFA for allegedly orchestrating a boycott.
details: X Corp. and the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA) have officially settled a multiyear legal dispute. The agreement marks the end of X's aggressive legal action against the WFA, which X had accused of orchestrating an illegal boycott of the platform.

The lawsuit stemmed from X's claim that advertisers, including major brands like Mars, CVS Health, Shell, and Lego, significantly reduced their spending on the platform following Elon Musk's takeover in 2022. X alleged that this decline was due to guidelines set by the WFA's Global Alliance for Responsible Media (GARM).

Advertisers had expressed concerns that their brands might appear alongside harmful content on X after Musk altered the platform's content moderation policies. The WFA and its affiliated advertisers rejected X's allegations, asserting their right to choose where to allocate their advertising budgets.

A federal court had previously dismissed X's lawsuit in March, ruling that the company failed to demonstrate harm under federal competition laws. X appealed this decision in April, but the settlement now puts this litigation behind both organizations.

In a joint statement, both X and the WFA emphasized their shared commitment to freedom of speech. The WFA also confirmed that it has discontinued GARM and will not restart similar initiatives, stating that brand-safety innovation will benefit brands, platforms, and consumers alike.
